1.translation: A challenger asked for a punishment bound to come[1]
1.footnotes: [1] In the Hereafter. The pagans of Makkah had challenged the Prophet (ﷺ) in ridicule by asking Allah to bring upon them His punishment. See 8:32.

2.translation: upon the disbelievers, which none can avert,

3.translation: from Allah, Lord of the pathways of ascent,

4.translation: by which the angels and the Spirit[2] will ascend to Him on a Day[3] the length of which is fifty thousand years.
4.footnotes:
[2] i.e., the angel Gabriel.
 [3] The Day of Judgment will be an extremely long day.

5.translation: So be patient [O Prophet] with beautiful patience.

6.translation: Indeed, they see this [punishment] far off,

7.translation: but We see it to be close at hand.

8.translation: On the Day when the sky will be like molten brass[4]

9.translation: and the mountains will be like dyed wool[5],

10.translation: and no close friend will ask about another,

11.translation: even though they will see one another. The wicked will wish he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by offering his children,

12.translation: and his wife and his brother,

13.translation: and his kindred who stood by him,

14.translation: and everyone on earth, just to save himself.

15.translation: By no means![6] It is a raging Flame,
15.footnotes: [6] An emphatic denial, meaning "It will never be."

16.translation: that will strip off the scalps[7].
16.footnotes: [7] Referring to the skin of the head or of the body extremities, which will be burned away by severe heat and flames.

17.translation: It will call everyone who turned their backs and disobeyed,

20.translation: when evil befalls him, he bewails,

21.translation: but when good fortune comes his way, he becomes tight-fisted –

23.translation: who are steadfast in their prayers;

24.translation: and who give a due share[8] of their wealth

25.translation: to the beggar and the dispossessed;

26.translation: and who firmly believe in the Day of Judgment;

27.translation: and those who fear the punishment of their Lord –

28.translation: for none can feel secure from their Lord’s punishment –

29.translation: and those who guard their private parts[9],
29.footnotes: [9] i.e., their chastity and honor from immoralities.

30.translation: except from their wives or bondwomen[10] whom they own, for then they are not to be blamed.

31.translation: But whoever seeks beyond that, it is they who are the transgressors.

32.translation: and those who fulfill their trusts and pledges;

33.translation: and who are upright in their testimonies;

34.translation: and who take due care of their prayers;

35.translation: they will be honored in gardens[11].

36.translation: What is the matter with the disbelievers that they are rushing towards you [O Prophet][12],

37.translation: from the right and from the left, in crowds[13]?
37.footnotes: [13] Some pagans of Makkah gathered around the Prophet (ﷺ) mocking and opposing him, claiming that if there is in fact a Hereafter, they would enter Paradise before the believers.

38.translation: Does everyone of them aspire to enter a garden of bliss?

39.translation: By no means! We have created them from what they know[14].

40.translation: I swear by the Lord of the sunrises and sunsets[15] that We are surely Capable
40.footnotes: [15] i.e., Allah is the One Who determines the daily points of sunrise and sunset according to each season by the rotation of the earth around its axis.

41.translation: to replace them with others better than them, and none can escape Our decree.

42.translation: So leave them to engage in their falsehood and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised;

43.translation: the Day when they will rush out of their graves as if they are racing towards an idol[16],
43.footnotes: [16] i.e., just as they used to race towards a newly appointed idol, to be among the first of its worshipers.

44.translation: with their eyes downcast and overwhelmed with disgrace. That is the Day that they were promised.
